items.text: Guardrail/SCP changes deployed and replication confirmed unbroken afterwards
items.why: Org guardrails silently break replication; an SCP change last Tuesday can mean a replication rule that has been failing ever since.
items.proof: Replication confirmed healthy on every mechanism after the 2026-09-03 SCP rollout; change ticket ACME-SEC-118 linked

items.text: Every replication path checked today and reporting current
items.why: Enabled is not working. Aurora global lag, S3 CRR status, ECR rules, replica secrets, backup copy age and the vendor recovery points each fail silently and in their own way — and current lag is your RPA if the event is now.
items.proof: Per-mechanism check dated 2026-09-12: global lag <1s, CRR COMPLETED, ECR current, replicas present, 0 errors on the vendor dashboard, 2 warnings triaged

items.text: Secret lists reconciled into ONE signed-off list
items.why: The August test died on the disagreement between the secrets actually marked for replication, the spreadsheet, and the runtime logical names.
items.proof: signed-off-secrets.csv v1 signed by claims + platform leads (pending platform signature)

items.text: Known blocker secrets readable BY THE APP ROLE in the recovery region
items.why: Existence is not access. The Sep 3 failure was secrets-init, and a secret can exist while KMS or the app role denies the read.
items.proof: get-secret-value run as the workload identity returns a value; sts get-caller-identity shows the app role

items.text: Drill containment ON, with VPC endpoints in place for ECR/Secrets Manager
items.why: Containment is the guard that stops a drill reaching real partners. Egress is solved with endpoints, not by removing containment (dec_sandbox_v2).
items.proof: No route from the recovery VPC to partner endpoints; endpoint list includes the S3 gateway endpoint; vendor sandbox on for the resources it recovers

items.text: Recovery coverage re-confirmed: every Tier-0 resource has a named mechanism
items.why: Coverage drifts: new services appear with no replication rule, old ones go stale. A bucket created last month is not in a CRR rule written last year, and a queue nobody added to scope comes back empty or not at all.
items.proof: Coverage review dated within a week of 2026-09-25: every Tier-0 component has a replication.mechanism and it matches what is actually configured in the account

items.text: Operator AND approver on the calendar for the full window
items.why: A test without its approver stalls at every gate.
items.proof: Invites accepted for 2026-09-25 09:00–16:00 by operator and DR lead

items.text: Partner contact confirmed with a test transaction ready
items.why: The success bar is a business transaction; without the partner-shaped test claim you cannot prove L6.
items.proof: Partner integration engineer confirmed; test-claim.json in the dr-tests repo

items.text: SSO/VPN access profiles to the recovery account tested by each operator
items.why: Discovering at T0 that nobody's credentials work in the recovery account is the most avoidable failure there is.
items.proof: Both operators ran sts get-caller-identity against the recovery account this week

items.text: DR readiness dashboard exists and the runbook's gates can be read from it
items.why: Every verify step needs somewhere to look; grepping logs under time pressure is not a dashboard.
items.proof: Dashboard v0 link; gate-to-panel mapping (tracked as gap_dash1 — not built yet)

items.text: Test plan written and T0 definition agreed
items.why: If T0 is not defined in advance, the RTA number gets negotiated after the fact — and nobody trusts a negotiated number.
items.proof: Test #3 plan doc: T0 = the first failover action (the recovery-region apply); success bar and roles named

items.text: Open data-path questions answered (Kinesis, Redis pharmacy, region-bound bucket names, the un-backfilled S3 objects)
items.why: Every 'does the app actually need X to answer a claim?' left open becomes a mid-test debugging session.
items.proof: gap_kinesis1 and gap_redis1 answered in writing; bucket-name config audit done; S3 Batch Replication backfill either run or explicitly deferred

items.text: Recovery-region quota and capacity headroom confirmed
items.why: A pilot light fails at scale-up when the account has no room for the instances, IPs or ENIs the full load needs. This is the most likely real failure and the slowest to fix mid-event.
items.proof: Service Quotas checked for EC2/EKS/RDS/NAT/EIP in the recovery region against full production load

items.text: IaC pipeline green and a recovery-region plan shows no drift
items.why: If the shape is restored from git, git has to be correct. Drift means the plan rebuilds something different from what production runs.
items.proof: terraform/terragrunt plan for the recovery region reports no changes

items.text: Runbook freshness: reviewed since the last infrastructure change
items.why: A runbook is a hypothesis about a system that keeps moving. Stale steps waste the minutes you cannot spare.
items.proof: Runbook updatedAt is newer than the last change to the components it names
